He currently lives and works in Beijing, as professor and master instructor of School of Experimental Art at CAFA，research of Chinese Arts and Crafts Institute of Prince Kung’ s Palace Museum, member of the Academic Committee of Beijing Zoo.

In recent years, his works have attended Live and Let Live: Creators of Tomorrow—The 4th Fukuoka Asian Art Triennial (Fukuoka Asian Art Museum, Fukuoka, Japan, 2009), Mind in Landscape (The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, Washington DC, USA, 2011), ALLES UNTER DEM HIMMEL GEHORT ALLEN: Chinese Public Art in Kassel (Kassel, Germany, 2012), Cosmos (Shanghai 21st Century Minsheng Art Museum, Shanghai, China, 2014), The Carolyn Hsu and René Balcer Collection: Exploring Three Decades of Contemporary Chinese Art (Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, USA, 2015), Lunar New Year: The Year of the Monkey (Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York City, USA, 2016), Continuum: Generation by Generation (The 57th Venice Biennale China Pavilion, Virgin Garden, Venice, Italy, 2017), Serpenti Form (Art Science Museum, Singapore, Singapore; Mori Art Gallery, Tokyo, Japan, 2017), Echigo-Tsumari Art Triennial 2018 (Echigo-Tsumari, Japan, 2018), etc. He has held several solo exhibitions in Beijing, Shanghai, Hong Kong and New York City.

Wu Jian’an’s works are in the collection of Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, Los Angeles County Museum Of Art, Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art, Cornell University, Oscar Niemeyer Museum, Central Academy of Fine Arts Museum, Beijing Minsheng Art Museum and Asia Art Archives, etc.

1764468870040653824.description:
2024年3月1日在北京开始孵一只受精的鸡蛋。拍摄这只蛋每日孵化的照片，将照片同步上传，直到21天小鸡孵出，或是孵化失败。现实世界一个生命的生成演化，同步于数字世界，得到一个数字孪生的生命。

On March 1, 2024, in Beijing, a fertilized chicken egg began incubating. Photos of the egg's daily incubation process will be taken and uploaded synchronously until either the chick hatches after 21 days or the incubation fails. The real-world birth and evolution of a life sync with its digital counterpart, creating a digital twin of life.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
邬建安的《蛋生》是纯粹对生命奇迹的观察和记录，艺术家将观察的过程，与数字世界同步，即艺术家试图讨论数字孪生的关系。作品还在人工干预、科技批判等领域埋下伏笔。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于邬建安更像倒置的关系，超人的存在，已经在他的作品中有暗喻，即掌控生命的进程，蛋生也可被理解为创生。未来也许是这样被设计和改变的，人类自己设计的多重可能性，并在自己设计的未来中被创造。

希望邬建安的作品能让你也去体会生命的奇迹，理解自己从何而来，理解生命脆弱、短暂、不可知。同时，也希望你能感受到艺术家对数字孪生、创生的超人思考，留一些空间。因为我们的生命正在转型期，与科技的接驳，将会构成新的伦理关系，将会孕育新的生命形态。

Wu Jian'an's "The Birth of the Egg" is a pure observation and documentation of the miracle of life. The artist synchronizes the process of observation with the digital world, aiming to explore the relationship of digital twins. The work also sets the stage for artificial intervention and critique of technology.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme is reversed in relation to Wu Jian'an. The existence of superhumans is already metaphorically implied in his work, representing the control of the process of life. "The Birth of the Egg" can also be understood as creation. The future may be designed and altered in such a way, with multiple possibilities created by humans within their own designed future.

It is hoped that Wu Jian'an's work will allow you to experience the miracle of life, understanding where you came from and the fragility, transience, and unknowability of life. At the same time, it is also hoped that you can appreciate the artist's contemplation of digital twins and the creation of superhumans, leaving space for interpretation. Because our lives are undergoing a transition period, intersecting with technology will form new ethical relationships and give birth to new forms of life.

1764468870040653824.artist_bio:
邬建安，1980年生于北京，祖籍上海金山。

现为中央美术学院实验艺术学院教授、硕士研究生导师，文化部恭王府中华传统技艺研究与保护中心研究员，北京动物园学术委员会委员。

近年来，邬建安的作品先后参加《越后妻有大地艺术三年展》（日本新泻越后妻有，2018）、第57届威尼斯双年展中国馆《不息》（意大利威尼斯，2017）、《蛇形》（日本东京森美术馆；新加坡艺术科学博物馆，2017）、《亚洲艺术部成立百年猴年新春特别项目》（美国纽约大都会艺术博物馆，2016）、《三十年的中国当代艺术：卡罗琳与雷内收藏展》（美国波士顿美术博物馆，2015）、《多重宇宙：民生二十一世纪美术馆开馆展》（上海民生二十一世纪美术馆，2014）、《大道之行：中国当代公共艺术展》（德国卡塞尔，2012）、《山水意园：中国当代艺术展》（美国华盛顿肯尼迪艺术中心，2011）、《共再生——第四届福冈亚洲三年展》（日本福冈亚洲美术馆，2009），并在北京、上海、香港、纽约等地举办多次个人艺术展。

美国波士顿美术博物馆、美国洛杉矶艺术博物馆、美国康奈尔大学赫伯特 F. 约翰逊艺术博物馆、巴西奥斯卡·尼迈耶博物馆、中央美术学院美术馆、北京民生现代美术馆、香港亚洲艺术文献库、澳大利亚白兔艺术基金会等机构和个人收藏有邬建安的作品。

他获得的主要艺术奖项包括“2017年度青年力量”（《南方人物周刊》）、“2018年度40 Under 40亚洲卓越艺术家”（Perspective《视野》杂志）、“第11届中国艺术权力榜 ——Art Power 100”、“第8届全球华人金星奖——年度中坚力量”（《国家美术》）等。

1771540611829207040.description:
32-3-904545-1 来自一个非常严谨的几何图案，32个平面直角等腰三角形密拼成一个正方形 [1]

将每个三角形变成三角拱，由于三角形大小不同导致拱的高度不同，原本在二维上严密的图形在三维上出现了缝隙，也就有了空间，结构，光，风…… 有了建筑的属性。艺术家在这里希望讨论可控复杂性的问题，也就是如何在极其严谨的数学规则中发现或创造有趣的带有某种属性的复杂性。

32-3-904545-1 comes from a very precise geometric pattern, 32 plane isosceles right triangles are closely packed into a square [1].

By turning each triangle into a triangular shell, Gaps appear in the three-dimensional space, the space, structure, light, wind... make it an architecture. The artists want to discuss the issue of organized complexity here, that is, how to discover or create interesting complexity with certain properties within extremely rigorous mathematical rules.

参考：
Reference:

1：Tilings by Isosceles Right Triangles，32:2007AA(GHM)
http://www.squaring.net/tritri/irts/irts.html

1768923618676445184.description:
T-bit听上去像是TIBET的谐音，我们都知道这和西藏的历史吐蕃有关，但是我发现Ti-bet这个称呼和我们今天的网络时代和大数据密切相关。也许是巧合，也许它意味西藏的未来和数据化紧密相连。是的我故意让其有着一个发音上的联系，但更深层次的原因是计算机和通信以及数据流
 
我曾经是一个IT工程师
 
T确实代表了西藏，而BIT有着多重的含义
比特（BIT，Binary digit），是计算机专业术语，是信息量单位，是由英文BIT音译而来。同时也是二进制数字中的位通常用于0和1的表达，是信息量的度量单位，也是信息量的最小单位。bit就是计算机内部数据存储的最小单位。
 
 因此我们可以故名思议，T-BIT就是西藏最小的信息量单位。
当然从英语字面理解 也可以将T-BIT理解为关于西藏的一个超大数据平台
，也可以用来表示一个简单的正/负的判断，比如有两种状态的开和关
甚至导线上电压的有无，一个抽像的逻辑上的然与否，等等。
  在数字洪流涌动的当下，人人都是摄影师，人人都是纪录者，人人也都是最小信息量的生产者，使用者，和流通者，我当然也是其中之一。而对庞大复杂的西藏，没有人可以解释，但人人都在试图解释。我们当然不可能在当下，用几张或几十张作品来解释西藏。我们到底在创作，还是在纪录？从另一个维度看，T-BIT 让我所有的拍摄和凝视，变成了数据流中的一个个环节，将这些行为变得有意义，这些纪录，将所有的拍摄，都变得有意义。
 
我在西藏漫游的日子，漫长且有趣，我发现了一件非常有趣的事：相比大多数区域那种小县城，或小乡镇适用的马斯洛需求层次，什么是动物性的，什么是人性的需求，在西藏并不完全适用。因为，越是在西藏偏远的地方，人们的精神生活反而更丰富。
 
我热爱记录那些美好，可是，当我真正面对时，我发现，用任何一种形式去表达，都非常片面、局部。且困惑！拍摄、纪录之后，是什么？
 
所有的拍摄和纪录都源自于个人化的观察，这导致了表达的片面性和局部性。我从没敢去举办任何一场个人的关于西藏的展览。20年来，我拍摄的那些，关于西藏的素材，照片就有数十万张，还有大量的视频和声音素材。可这都是片段。
 
当我终于明白，片段中的每一个瞬间，最多也只是构成“西藏”的一个像素的时候，我懂得了《T-bit》对于这个时代，对于我的——意义。
 
《T-bit》是我对非物质性，对人性、社群、文化传承、地缘的思考，也是对数字技术带来的诸多问题的尝试和回应。这是我精神何处安放的尝试。
 
以数十万张照片为像素基础，重构“布达拉宫”，作为地景艺术《T-bit》的开始。2023年10月6日揭幕仪式之后，我将带着《T-bit》，去到那些曾经感动、温暖、帮助过我，那些工作过、观察过的地方。在冈仁波齐、札达、古格、山南雍布拉康、南迦巴瓦、珠峰以及羌塘无人区……去完成时间、空间、人，和一切生灵的对话，并再次记录。
 
西藏，是点亮我内心的——光！
 
千百年来，每当夜幕降临，布达拉宫的雄姿，就隐没在夜色中，西藏的电力开始于1928年，布达拉宫闪耀在夜间也是近几十年的变化。
 
《T-bit》是一个自发光体，我将以此去呼应当下的布达拉宫。西藏必将在新科技下面临的新挑战，在技术跃升带来困扰的同时，也同时带来传播上的扩展。《T-bit》希望完成一次集合计算机编程、光、流动性、元宇宙、地景等诸多方面的尝试。
 
而西藏，就是光，会一直引领着我。

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
卡布的《T-Bit》是图像考古作品，来自艺术家20年来的创作，卡布将图像再次创作成像素画的风格，完成新的数字拼贴。卡布将这个项目带回之前走过的道路和拍摄地，与当地的人、动物、大地、天空分享。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于卡布的作品《T-Bit》，是另一种延伸关系。数字化的图像，大自然中的生命，奇迹般的，数字平权。卡布的行动，及其扭曲的场域关系，恰是技术和自然并峙的现状。

希望卡布的的作品，能让你思考自然和科技是否冲突，以及如何改变和应对这一冲突。希望你也可以像卡布一样，去很远的地方旅行，在山中，在林中，在旷野中，为未来设问。

Khabu's "T-Bit" is an artistic exploration of image archaeology, drawing from the artist's 20 years of creative work. Khabu recreates images in a pixelated style, completing new digital collages. The project brings Khabu back to the paths and shooting locations previously traversed, sharing them with the local people, animals, land, and sky.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme relates to Khabu's work "T-Bit" in an extended sense. Digitalized images, life in nature, miraculously, and digital equality. Khabu's actions and distorted field relationships aptly represent the current juxtaposition of technology and nature.

It is hoped that Khabu's work will prompt you to contemplate whether nature and technology are in conflict, as well as how to change and respond to this conflict. Hopefully, you can, like Khabu, travel to faraway places, in the mountains, in the forests, in the wilderness, and question the future.

1771024242536747008.description: 空间中用肉眼看，没有作品。用我们今天观看世界的“主要方式” 手机或者IPAD屏幕看那片空间，有一个撑满空间的大铁球，观众举着手机通过调整自己与作品的距离和角度来观看作品的局部或者整体。于此同时，观众扫描二维码给手机按上准备好的软件，通过纸媒或者网络传播，让更多的人足不出户就可以在家里360度观看这件雕塑作品。Space with the naked eye, no works. We use the "main way" of viewing the world today, mobile phone or IPAD screen to look at that space, there is a big iron ball that fills the space, and the audience holds the mobile phone to watch the part or the whole of the work by adjusting the distance and Angle between themselves and the work. At the same time, the audience can scan the QR code and press the prepared software on the mobile phone to spread through the paper media or the Internet, so that more people can watch the sculpture in 360 degrees at home without leaving the house.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
张增增的《无形之形》完成于2014年，正值VR、AR、MR讨论大热的时期，是另一件元宇宙这一概念的先导性作品。艺术家在讨论数字世界无形的入侵关系，是对城市景观的介入，也是对数字时代到来的担忧。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于张增增的作品《无形之形》，是接续关系。数字化的风景，与真实的风景和人，构成了一个整体。《无形之形》是未来的预言之一，尝试改变现在的，也恰是来自未来的想象力。

希望张增增的作品，能让你试着思考如何在未来生活，一切图像的真实和虚拟，也许会合而为一，你会有数字分身，会在不同的场景中，跳入跳出。如同科幻作品中，探讨的时空旅行者的困境，因为过度兴奋，可能会让你失眠。

Zhang Zengzeng's "Invisible Form" was completed in 2014, during the height of discussions on VR, AR, and MR, and is another pioneering work exploring the concept of the metaverse. The artist explores the intangible invasion of the digital world, intervening in urban landscapes and expressing concerns about the advent of the digital age.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme relates to Zhang Zengzeng's work "Invisible Form" in a continuum. The digitalized scenery, along with real landscapes and people, form a cohesive whole. "Invisible Form" is one of the prophecies of the future, attempting to change the present while drawing on imaginative visions from the future.

It is hoped that Zhang Zengzeng's work will prompt you to contemplate how to live in the future. The convergence of real and virtual images may result in a merging of the two, where you might have a digital avatar, capable of jumping in and out of different scenarios. Similar to the dilemmas faced by time travelers in science fiction, excessive excitement about such possibilities may even make you lose sleep.

1771024242536747008.artist_bio:
张增增，男，2013年毕业于四川美术学院雕塑系获硕士学位，多年致力于科技手段与城市三维空间之结合，试图将不可见的哲学和社会逻辑可视化、三维化。努力使得作品尺寸超越小物体，造境取代消极造物，从图像而至现象，由场所到城市，从小范围的有限个人感知抵达无边无尽的空间。在过去十余年中进行了一系列美术馆内外的研究，有关新的材料学，空间技术和城市现象。从城市、景观、室内、公共关系各角度展开的跨学科研究。现任教于四川美术学院雕塑系跨媒介工作室。
Zhang Zengzeng, male, graduated from the Sculpture Department of Sichuan Fine Arts Institute in 2013 with a master's degree. For many years, he has devoted himself to the combination of scientific and technological means and urban three-dimensional space, trying to visualize and three-dimensional invisible philosophy and social logic.
Strive to make the size of the work beyond small objects, create environment instead of negative creation, from images to phenomena, from places to cities, from limited personal perception on a small scale to endless space.
Over the past ten years, a series of research has been carried out both inside and outside the museum, concerning new materials science, space technology and urban phenomena.
Interdisciplinary research from the perspectives of city, landscape, interior and public relations.
He is currently teaching at the cross-media Studio of Sculpture Department, Sichuan Fine Arts Institute.

1767569417102823424.description:
从谷歌地图中位于新疆东部一处无人区的距离地面 10 公里的空中，可以 俯瞰到有 30 个巨大的中国字和 1 个感叹号盘桓在荒凉的戈壁上，每个字有一个 足球场那么大。这些大字是一些文革的口号，由碎石堆砌而成，在 1968 年这 里修建了一个秘密的军用机场，这些大字就是这个机场的航标。摄影机在这些 大字中穿行，在碎石堆积而成的乌托邦的幻觉里浮现出 1968 年世界各地的革 命浪潮，一些浪潮在开始，一些浪潮被熄灭⋯⋯ 
     Using Google Maps, one can look down from ten miles above upon a no-man’s land in eastern Xinjiang and see thirty enormous Chinese characters and an exclamation point twisting their way through the desolate Gobi Desert. Each character is the size of a football field and they form slogans from the Cultural Revolution, built with crushed stone. A secret military airport was built in just this spot in 1968, and these big characters served as its navigational markings. The camera makes its way through the characters, and there in the Utopian hallucination of the piled stones, the tidal wave of revolution that swept across the world in 1968 appears. Some waves were just beginning, while others were being extinguished....

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
雎安奇的《大字》完成于2015年，巨大的词句来自毛泽东先生的诗词，而这些诗词却在60年代作为军用，尤其是飞行员的航标。作品揭示一个时代的变化，尤其是技术升级之后，人在技术环境中，位置和身份的消逝。艺术家试着将当代艺术在同一时间探索的问题，与中国时间同步，让作品更深度的介入到地缘环境中，不同组织和文化环境中的人。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于雎安奇的作品《大字》，是历史维度的，由人贯穿的，巨大风景中的人之回响。此作品对时代、人和技术的反思，也可以被看作通往未来元宇宙的道路。

希望雎安奇的作品，能让你将今天的现实，放在过去的、历史的维度中，思考过去和现在。艺术家带我们去的无人之境，遗落的基地，那些曾经留下痕迹人。也许现在的时代，在地球的某处存在的人。是否也可能会在元宇宙的世界中，与你相遇。

Ju Anqi's "Big Characters" was completed in 2015, featuring massive words and phrases taken from the poetry of Chairman Mao Zedong. Interestingly, these poetic texts were used as military symbols in the 1960s, particularly for pilots. The artwork reveals the changes in an era, especially the disappearance of one's position and identity in the technological environment after technological upgrades. The artist attempts to synchronize the contemporary art exploration with the timeline of China, allowing the work to deeply engage with the geopolitical environment and the people within different organizations and cultural contexts.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of Ju Anqi's work "Giant Characters" takes on a historical dimension, intertwined with human beings and resonating within vast landscapes. This artwork's reflection on the era, humanity, and technology can also be seen as a path leading to the future metaverse.

It is hoped that Ju Anqi's work will prompt you to place today's reality within the context of the past and history and contemplate the connection between the past and the present. The artist takes us to deserted places, abandoned bases, where traces of people were once left. Perhaps the people existing somewhere on Earth in the present era might also encounter you in the world of the metaverse.

1767569417102823424.artist_bio: 雎安奇是目前备受国际瞩目的中国电影导演、艺术家之一。作品参加过超过40个国际影展，也曾于巴黎蓬皮杜中心、纽约现代艺术博物馆、纽约古根海姆美术馆等国际顶级艺术机构展出。电影处女作《北京的风很大》入围50届柏林国际电影节，2015年剧情片《诗人出差了》在第44届鹿特丹国际电影节首映并获得了最佳亚洲电影大奖，以及第16届韩国全州国际电影节最高大奖。最新剧情长片《海面上漂过的奖杯》在第3届平遥国际电影展获得三项大奖。2019年开始拍摄全球首部中国建筑遗产纪录片“中国建筑遗产三部曲”，2022年完成三部曲首部影片《楼》，入围第四届海南国际电影展，2022年度中国纪录片学院奖提名，第25届上海国际电影节，2023年第45届联合国教科文组织探索之星奖。2023年雎安奇担任了第25届上海国际电影节金爵奖评委。雎安奇亦是中国单色绘画的代表，其创作的《草体》绘画系列作品在亚洲的单色画创作领域中享有重要地位，作品呈现在全球众多的重量级展览，美术馆和艺术博览会上。

1769961595078840320.description:
怪力乱神出自《论语》，“子不语怪力乱力乱神。”这句话在当下有很多种解析，最为学术界所认同的解释应当是，孔子不谈论不在神谱上的鬼神。怪力乱神从字面意思亦指关于怪异、勇力、叛乱、鬼神之事。

这个项目延续了张晓对中国民间社会的持续关注。张晓之前的很多作品都是源自故乡，是围绕着民间的美学和审美对民间社会进行深入的探讨，而这次的创作则从故乡的农村扩展到了更大范围的中国乡村社会，去关注这些形式丰富的民间信仰。这些新造的神像千奇百怪，同时他们的形象也涉及到这个时代的各行各业，这些源于当下的塑像形象打破了宗教原有的信仰和审美体系，转而变成了老百姓需要什么就会塑一个与之对应的菩萨。

张晓并非在批判这种民间信仰和艳俗的形象，他更多的是去呈现这种当下的存在。这种民间信仰在中国的乡村社会极为普遍，或许这些民间信仰并不能代表一种宗教，或者说这是宗教在中国的经济发展过程中所产生的一种变异，他们大都是生硬和直接的，更多的是体现出一种民众的集体无意识。这也是民间底层社会对于宗教和信仰的需求，他们渴望从这里寻求心理安慰和心理暗示。这些神像给他们提供了一个粗糙又直白的载体，藉此希望找到生活的出口。尽管这些菩萨或许并不在神谱之上，亦为很多人避而不谈之事。

Guai Li Luan Shen (‘怪力乱神’) stems from a line in the Analects of Confucius, “The subjects on which the Master did not talk, were: extraordinary things, feats of strength, disorder, and spiritual beings.” (‘子不语怪力乱力乱神’). There are many interpretations of this quotation today, but the most scholarly would be that Confucius did not talk about ghosts and gods that were not on the divine list. In a literal sense, the phrase Guai Li Luan Shen also refers to things about bizarreness, courage, rebellion as well as ghosts and gods. 

This project continues Zhang Xiao’s ongoing interest in Chinese folk society. While many of Zhang Xiao’s previous works originated in his hometown and explored folk society in depth around folk aesthetics and their appreciation of beauty, this project extends from the artist’s native place in the countryside to the larger Chinese rural society, focusing on the rich forms of Chinese folk religion. These newly created deities are exceedingly strange with their images corresponding to all walks of life in our time. The icons rooted in the present breaks down the original belief and aesthetic system of religion and turn into ad-hoc bodhisattvas that embody whatever the people desire. 

Zhang Xiao is not criticizing this kind of folk religion and kitsch images; he merely tries to lay out their current existence. Forms of folk religion as such are pervasive in China’s rural society, which probably do not compose a religion in the strict sense or can be rather understood as a religious mutation in the process of China’s economic development. The imagery is primarily raw and direct, reflecting more of a collective unconscious of the people. At the same time, it also speaks to the need for religion and faith from the civil underclass, who are eager to seek psychological comfort and suggestion from the divine. The statues provide the people with a crude and straightforward vehicle to navigate and find a way out in their lives – although these bodhisattvas may not be on the divine list and are hardly mentioned by the believers.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
张晓的《键盘侠菩萨》是这几年，艺术家与木雕匠人合作的作品。类似《美国众神》（American Gods, 2001）小说中描述的，旧神被新神取代。彩塑的木雕则来自特别细微的日常需求，如《键盘侠菩萨》是否应该保佑那些驰骋网络的意见者？

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于张晓的作品《键盘侠菩萨》，是日常而温情的，类似微小精神需要的具体化。而艺术家试着代入不同人群的价值观，及其信仰。

希望张晓的作品，能让你关注到文化和社群的多样性，进入到不同社群的视野，想象一下，一起进入到未来元宇宙的，也可能是人类整体，因相互补偿而共存。

Zhang Xiao's "Keyboard Man Bodhisattva" is a collaborative artwork between the artist and woodcarvers in recent years. Similar to the depiction in the novel "American Gods" (2001), where the old gods are replaced by new gods, the colorful wooden sculptures in this artwork stem from specific and subtle daily needs. For example, should the "Keyboard Man Bodhisattva" bless those who express their opinions freely on the internet?

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of Zhang Xiao's work "Keyboard Man Bodhisattva" takes on a daily and heartfelt tone, representing the materialization of small spiritual needs. The artist attempts to embody the values and beliefs of different communities by stepping into their shoes.

It is hoped that Zhang Xiao's work will draw your attention to the diversity of cultures and communities, allowing you to enter the perspectives of different social groups. Imagine coming together in the future metaverse, where the coexistence of humanity as a whole is made possible through mutual understanding and compensation.

1769961595078840320.artist_bio:
张晓

1981年出生于山东烟台，2005年毕业于烟台大学建筑设计系。在2009年成为摄影艺术家之前，他曾于《重庆晨报》担任新闻摄影记者。2018年，张晓获得哈佛大学罗伯特·加德纳摄影基金。张晓的《海岸线》系列曾获得法国汇丰银行摄影奖（2011）、法国才华摄影基金中国区冠军（2010）及候登科摄影奖（2009），《他们》系列则在2010年获得三影堂摄影奖大奖。张晓曾参与哈佛大学皮博迪考古和民族学博物馆的展览“社火”，UCCA尤伦斯当代艺术中心的展览“2015年作为理由”和“文明：当代生活启示录”。及瑞士摄影基金会的“Unfamiliar Familiarities”和法国巴黎布朗利码头博物馆的“Photoquai 2015”，以及连州摄影博物馆的个展《苹果》，上海摄影艺术中心《摄寻千里：十见天日》，成都麓湖A4美术馆《2000年以来的西南影像实验》，chi k11艺术空间《农场》等在内的多个国内外展览，张晓现工作生活于成都。

Zhang Xiao

Born in 1981 in Yantai city, Shandong province, China, Zhang Xiao graduated from the Department of Architecture and Design at Yantai University in 2005. He was a photojournalist for Chongqing Morning Post. Zhang won the Robert Gardner Fellow in Photography of Harvard University in 2018. He won the Three Shadows Photography Award in 2010 with They series. He also received the second Hou Dengke Documentary Photography Award in 2009, The Photography Talent Award (France) in 2010 and the Prix HSBC pour la Photographie in 2011 with his Coastline series. Zhang has participated in several solo and group exhibitions, including “Shehuo”, Harvard University Peabody Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology,  “ The World in 2015 ”, “Civilization: The Way We Live Now”( Ullens Centre for Contemporary Art, Beijing, China),    “ Unfamiliar Familiarities ” , ( Fotostiftung Schweiz ,Winterthur, Switzerland), “ Photoquai ”， ( Quai Branly Museum，Paris，France ),  and “ Apple ”, ( Lianzhou Photography Museum, Guangdong, China), “ Social Geography: Ten Journeys with a Camera , (Shanghai Centre of Photography ,Shanghai , China) , “ Photography and Video Experiments in Southwestern China since 2000 ” , (A4 Art Museum ,Chengdu , China) , “The Farm”, (chi k11 Art Space, Shenyang, China), etc. Zhang currently lives and works in Chengdu city, Sichuan province, China.

1770014400623808512.description:
棕丝为材料的装置作品是我一直持续到现在的一个系列，从选材到制作是一个漫长的过程，将棕榈叶片撕成棕丝，制作成一系列的生活物品，细看这些物品是一些“残缺”“非正常”的生活之物，作品以一种“未完成”的状态呈现出一个唯美与诗意的现场，背后却是廉价与平俗，正如理想与现实。在每一次与材料接触的过程都像是进行一场博弈，在控制与放任之间拿捏分寸，我试图让自己达到一种由技入道的状态，将“重”隐藏在“轻”之下。The installation works made of palm silk are a series that I have been working on until now. From material selection to production, it is a long process. Palm leaves are torn into palm silk and made into a series of daily objects.
Behind it is cheap and common, just like ideal and reality.
In every process of contact with materials is like a game, between control and laissez-faire, I try to let myself reach a state of technology into the road, the "heavy" hidden under the "light".

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
李娜的《异场》是艺术家十几年长期工作的线索，丝线状态下，显现出的任何形态，都可以被看作建筑的空间和场域。艺术家《异场》，还在讨论一些似是而非的关系，那些被确认为女性主义，或女性艺术特征的东西，也可以被看作文化异化的场域。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于李娜的作品《异场》，有着巨大的能量，时间流逝中，艺术家选择不懈的工作。在反向思考材料和时间的意义，反向思考性别和生命维度的意义。

希望李娜的工作，能让你重拾材料和美的认识，让日常的每一刻，都是劳作和努力的美感。

Li Na's "Different Field" is a culmination of the artist's long-term work spanning over a decade. Under the state of silk threads, any form that emerges can be regarded as the spatiality and domain of architecture. In her work "Different Field," the artist also explores some paradoxical relationships, where things identified as feminist or bearing characteristics of women's art can also be seen as fields of cultural estrangement.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of Li Na's work "Different Field" holds immense power. As time flows, the artist tirelessly engages in her work. It involves a reverse contemplation of the significance of materials and time, as well as a reverse contemplation of the significance of gender and dimensions of life.

It is hoped that Li Na's work will allow you to rediscover the understanding of materials and beauty, making every moment of daily life a source of aesthetic labor and effort.

1770014400623808512.artist_bio:
2013年毕业于四川美术学院雕塑系 获硕士学位
2018年 意大利佛罗伦萨国际青年艺术家驻留项目
现任教于四川美术学院 雕塑系
专注于对材料与跨媒介领域的探索实践。曾获“新感知-未知的爱”--优秀女性艺术家奖、中国雕塑大展青年新锐奖、“明天”雕塑奖，作品被北京今日美术馆、北京时代美术馆、坪山美术馆、湖北美术馆、四川美术学院美术馆等收藏。
In 2013, he graduated from the sculpture Department of Sichuan Fine Arts Institute with a master's degree
2018 International Young Artist Residency Program in Florence, Italy
He is currently teaching at the Sculpture Department of Sichuan Fine Arts Institute
Focus on the exploration and practice of materials and cross-media fields.
He has won the "New Perception - Unknown Love" - Outstanding Female Artist Award, China Sculpture Exhibition Young Talent Award, "Tomorrow" sculpture Award, and his works are collected by Beijing Today Art Museum, Beijing Times Art Museum, Pingshan Art Museum, Hubei Art Museum, Sichuan Fine Arts Institute Art Museum, etc.

1769408131835760640.description:
《红、黄、蓝的构成生成器》是一件通过代码模拟皮特·蒙德里安《红、黄、蓝的构成》创作的，探索色彩与形状无限组合可能性的数字艺术作品。

作品基于迭代分割、随机性与概率权重等基本数学原理创作，每次页面访问都会即时生成新的构图，确保每位收藏者获得的版本都是独一无二的。该作品限量发行1万份。此作品于2012年创作，作为我在伦敦大学金匠学院运算艺术专业中艺术家编程课程的一个项目，它反映了我在编程和创意表达方面的早期探索。蒙德里安生成器也是很多 Processing 创意编程课的一个阶段作业。

为本次展览及BTC区块链销售，我将作品由 processing 1.5版本升级至 p5.js。p5.js是加密艺术和生成艺术在Artblocks平台上最广泛使用的编程库。

"The Composition Generator of Red, Yellow, and Blue" is a digital art piece inspired by Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Yellow, and Blue." It explores the infinite possibilities of color and shape combinations using code. The artwork is based on fundamental mathematical principles such as iterative division, randomness, and probability weights, generating new compositions with each page visit. The artwork is code-based, while the artwork being exhibited and sold is a unique recorded version.

This work was created in 2012 as part of a project for the Artist Programming course in the Computational Arts program at Goldsmiths, University of London. It reflects my early exploration in programming and creative expression. The Mondrian Generator has also become a common assignment in many Processing creative programming courses.

For this exhibition and BTC blockchain sale, I upgraded the work from Processing 1.5 to p5.js. p5.js is the most widely used programming library for crypto art and generative art on the Artblocks platform.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
周姜杉的作品《红、黄、蓝的构成生成器》，是一件基于网络生成的艺术创作，完成于2012年。作品探索生成的随机性，以及艺术历史的可变性。艺术家成为这一无限可能框架的设计者。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于周姜杉的作品《红、黄、蓝的构成生成器》，是媒介更新后的再现，基于网络的、生成的，构成在加密线索中，更加永恒的新生。

希望周姜杉的作品，让你思考媒介批判的现实，如何认识到技术演化带来的更新，即是必然，也可能是有意识的选择。也许技术是你的朋友，你可以使用，并与之相处，让你的世界演化出多种可能。

Zhou Jiangshan's artwork "Composition Generator in Red, Yellow, and Blue" is a web-based generative art piece created in 2012. The work explores the randomness of generation and the variability of art history. The artist becomes the designer within this framework of infinite possibilities.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of Zhou Jiangshan's work "Composition Generator in Red, Yellow, and Blue" represents a reenactment after the update of media, based on the internet and generative processes. It creates a new form of eternal existence within encrypted clues.

It is hoped that Zhou Jiangshan's work will prompt you to contemplate the reality of media criticism and how to recognize the updates brought about by technological evolution, whether as an inevitability or a conscious choice. Perhaps technology can be your friend, with which you can interact and coexist, allowing your world to evolve into various possibilities.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
董师的作品《gold、city dog、⚖️》，是一件长期的、每天的、基于网络的数字艺术创作。作品均来自艺术家董师每天的一张绘画。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于董师的作品《gold、city dog、⚖️》，是基于绘画媒介在数字生成过程的转化，是基于传播理论，在社群蔓延的艺术之转向。是现在我们都在经历的媒介化挑战的现实，我们会从今天向着未来继续前行。

希望董师的作品，让你愉快的，每天能有可能，出现在你的社群和朋友圈，电子化的瞬间，可能在回望的时候，没有了痕迹。试着理解人创造的，也都将消失。

Dong Shi's artwork "gold, city dog, ⚖️" is a long-term, daily, web-based digital art creation. The works are derived from Dong Shi's daily paintings.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of Dong Shi's work "gold, city dog, ⚖️" represents a transformation of the painting medium into a digital generative process. It is based on theories of communication and represents a shift in art within the spread of social communities. It reflects the reality of the media challenges we are all experiencing, and we will continue moving towards the future from today.

It is hoped that Dong Shi's work will bring you joy and have the possibility of appearing in your social networks and friend circles every day. These electronic moments may leave no trace when looking back. Try to understand that what humans create will eventually disappear.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
毕竞的两件作品《A POEM》《GLASS MEMORY》都来自他学习时期（2016年前后）的动画，明显受到版画影响，作品很温柔和抒情。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于毕竞更像是一次记忆的旅程，是完全诗意和情感化的，对过去某一时刻的递归。在讨论残破不堪技术的时刻，也在反思今天的不完美。

希望毕竞的作品能让你回到诗意的，历史的某一刻。希望一切烦恼都能融化在时间中，如同一个梦。

Bi Jing's two works, "A POEM" and "GLASS MEMORY," both originate from his study period (around 2016) in animation and show clear influences from printmaking. The works are gentle, lyrical, and expressive.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of Bi Jing's work is more like a journey of memory, a fully poetic and emotional exploration of a specific moment in the past. It reflects on the imperfect technology of the time and prompts us to reflect on our own imperfections today.

It is hoped that Bi Jing's work will transport you back to a poetic and historical moment. May all your troubles melt away in the passage of time, like a dream.

1768159429129277440.artist_bio:
Bi Jing

1767810494317596672.description:
Glass Memory
动画
1’40”
2016

这件作品源于十多年前的一件用手持DV拍摄的习作，我用一个玻璃杯作为主角尝试了蒙太奇和长镜头的练习，直到其摔碎，那是我第一次接触到影像语言。现在这件习作已经丢失，留下的只有在我脑中零星模糊的几个画面，就像老DV的糟糕画质。<Glass Memory>是这件前作的“重制”，我试图从记忆的只言片语中挖掘更多的信息，但始终停留在某几个特定的画面上，想象似乎占据了主导，其余的记忆呈现出了一种中间状态，介于先验和日常，想象和记忆，虚拟和现实。就像光透过玻璃折射，水波泛起涟漪，你再看时，它们折叠、混合、扭动、异化出另一幅景象。

Glass Memory
Animation
1’40”
2016

This work can be traced back to an old work shot with a handheld DV more than ten years ago. The course of moving images brought me in contact with the language of film for the first time when I was in college. I made a work where a glass experienced a journey of “montage and long take” till smashing to pieces. The video has been lost only with some blurred images left in my mind，just like the poor images of the old DV. <Glass Memory> is a “resurrection” of the previous one. But the imagination dominates when I try to dig out more information from the fragments of memory. Only a few unstable mind images remain and the rest of memories show an in-between state living on the boundaries of transcendental experiences and daily lives, imagination and memories, virtual and actual. Just like light passing through glass and water rippling, when you look at them, they fold, blend, inflect, and alienate to create another scene.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
毕竞的两件作品《A POEM》《GLASS MEMORY》都来自他学习时期（2016年前后）的动画，明显受到版画影响，作品很温柔和抒情。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于毕竞更像是一次记忆的旅程，是完全诗意和情感化的，对过去某一时刻的递归。在讨论残破不堪技术的时刻，也在反思今天的不完美。

希望毕竞的作品能让你回到诗意的，历史的某一刻。希望一切烦恼都能融化在时间中，如同一个梦。

Bi Jing's two works, "A POEM" and "GLASS MEMORY," both originate from his study period (around 2016) in animation and show clear influences from printmaking. The works are gentle, lyrical, and expressive.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of Bi Jing's work is more like a journey of memory, a fully poetic and emotional exploration of a specific moment in the past. It reflects on the imperfect technology of the time and prompts us to reflect on our own imperfections today.

It is hoped that Bi Jing's work will transport you back to a poetic and historical moment. May all your troubles melt away in the passage of time, like a dream.

1767742458369806336.description:
The term “innumerable” often connotes repetition, whether it is in reference to time, information, wealth, possibilities, or expressions of gratitude, longing, and love. In each case, “innumerable” implies a sense of repetition, which suggests that perseverance ultimately leads to permanence—a quality we often cherish in life. While we appreciate permanence and persistence, repetition itself is not always welcomed.

Yet, it is often through the most mechanical and rigid repetition that we notice subtle variations and shifts. Gilles Deleuze argues that repetition breeds difference, laying the groundwork for innovation. So, what lies ahead for the future of visual arts: repetition or innovation? Reflecting on the decades since my birth in the 1970s, I see few groundbreaking innovations aside from the Internet. Visual arts are rife with repetition. There is repetition in modes of expression, materials, styles, and even the underlying concepts portrayed in artworks. Becoming a professional in any field requires accruing experience, often gained through repetition. Thus, an expert is essentially someone who embodies extensive repetition, functioning as an empiricist, a far cry from the realm of innovation.

Amid the vastness of the innumerable, uniformity often overshadows uniqueness. Roughly 80% of our personality is a pervasive uniformity that conceals our mediocrity. Within the multitude of innumerable individuals, we find a collective refuge, a respite from the omnipresent competition that permeates our existence. Life unfolds as a succession of innumerable sunrises, sunsets, moments of beauty, sips of wine, and challenges demanding our attention and effort. As the self-proclaimed rulers of the Earth, humans possess innumerable justifications for exploiting nature’s resources, yet seldom contemplate the innumerable other species inhabiting our planet and their innumerable cries of despair.

The diversity of human experience encompasses innumerable tender emotions, in which I place unwavering trust. The vast repository of information at our disposal harbors innumerable stories, each uniquely captivating. The notion of “innumerable” holds me spellbound, whisking me away to diverse realms with exhilarating speed, as if I can almost hear the wind rushing past my ears.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
何见平的作品《innumerable》，是一件空间作品，在上海誌屋空间的外墙，随风而动。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于何见平的作品《innumerable》，也许是空间之间的流转，一种不可见自然力推动的世界，也许这是何见平对现在动荡中世界的暗喻，也指向不确定的未来。

希望你能亲身体验何见平作品的空间关系，能让这个微小的视频带着你的思绪，到一个去处，在随风流动的作品前，体会物件尺度和空间，的自然关系。

He Jianping's artwork "innumerable" is a spatial installation located on the exterior wall of the Shanghainese House space in Shanghai. It moves with the wind, creating a dynamic experience.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the theme of He Jianping's work "innumerable" may represent the flow between spaces, a world propelled by invisible natural forces. It could be interpreted as He Jianping's metaphor for the turbulent world we live in today and also points towards an uncertain future.

It is hoped that you will have the opportunity to personally experience the spatial relationship in He Jianping's artwork, allowing the small video to take your thoughts to a place where you can feel the natural relationship between objects, scale, and space in front of this flowing artwork.

1766565128075087872.description: The "Metakaleidoscope series" aims to explore the vast realm of visual effects, presenting a unique aesthetic experience characterized by its use of repetitive and symmetrical patterns. This exploration seeks to delve into the endless possibilities of how patterns can be arranged and perceived, pushing the boundaries of traditional visual aesthetics. By leveraging the concept of a kaleidoscope, which traditionally uses mirrors and pieces of colored glass to create ever-changing patterns when turned, this series likely transcends the physical limitations to explore more abstract or digitally enhanced visual experiences.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
刘真辰的作品为一个视频《MetaKaleidoscope》和两个静态图像《MetaKaleidoscope_000》《MetaKaleidoscope_001》，来自其十几年前的视频观念和特效作品，在此复活。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于刘真辰的创作，有着自然递进的关系，刘真辰的工作即在讨论技术演化带来的新图像，及其技术背后的社会信息。社会信息在刘真辰的创作中，是输入图像的源头，也是艺术家关注的姿态。

希望你能在刘真辰的作品中，体会循环往复的美，在这个《原万花筒》的世界缅怀你的童年。

Liu Zhenchen's artwork consists of a video titled "MetaKaleidoscope" and two static images, "MetaKaleidoscope_000" and "MetaKaleidoscope_001." These pieces draw from his video concepts and special effects work from over a decade ago, bringing them back to life.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," Liu Zhenchen's creative work exhibits a natural progression. He explores the new imagery brought about by technological evolution and delves into the societal information behind these technologies. In Liu Zhenchen's work, societal information serves as the source of input imagery and reflects the artist's concerns.

It is hoped that you will experience the beauty of repetition in Liu Zhenchen's artwork and evoke memories of your childhood in this world of the "MetaKaleidoscope."

1766565128075087872.artist_bio:
Zhenchen Liu, lives and works between Paris and Shanghai. After studying painting and video at the Fine Arts College of Shanghai University and the Villa Arson - National Superior school of Arts in Nice, he received a “Post-Diplôme” at the Fresnoy - National Studio of Contemporary Arts in Tourcoing, France.
Last years, he has received a long list of awards and has presented his works on both film and visual arts platforms including Locarno Film Festival, Oberhausen Film Festival, Les Rencontres d’Arles Photo Festival, “Nuit Blanche” in Paris, Transmediale in Berlin, Ars Electronica in Linz, Grand Palais, Palais de Tokyo, Centre Pompidou in Paris, Kunst Museum Bonn, Contemporary Art Museum in Marseille, National Taiwan Museum of Fine Art... His work is included in the permanent collection of the Centre Pompidou.

1764822027295920128.description:
作品名称:直径 12.7 
影像 video 16:9 
作品简介: 在影像中出现的白碗实际直径是12.7厘米，而题目中只有数字没有单位。12.7的数字给观者留下的是一种想象，这种想象是以诗意对技术的一种消解。12.7可以无限大亦可以⽆无限小，其实无限大与无限小都是技术永远无法达到的。同时，这种对“无限”的想象如碗中的水，可见却又不可见。

Title: Diameter 12.7 
video 16:9 
Description: The actual diameter of the white bowl in the video is 12.7cm, but the title only contains a number and not a unit. 12.7 leaves the viewer with a kind of imagination, which is a kind of poetic dissolution of technology. 12.7 can be infinitely large or infinitely small, but in fact both infinity and infinity can never be achieved by technology. At the same time, this imagination of "infinity" is like water in a bowl, visible yet invisible.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
陈霄的作品《直径 12.7》，是艺术家创作的一件观念录像作品。如同禅宗的一些思绪，作品保持着对等待和偶然的张力，一瞬间水的波动，也许是心在动。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于陈霄的创作，更像是对过去的肯定，特别出离的瞬间，借助电子图像和显示器呈现的场景，也许是未来存在的悖论。

希望你能感受到陈霄作品中强大的心，以及突然出神的瞬间，动与不动，也许都在你的心中。

Chen Xiao's artwork "Diameter 12.7" is a conceptual video piece created by the artist. Like certain thoughts in Zen Buddhism, the work maintains a tension between waiting and chance. The momentary fluctuation of water may represent the movement of the heart.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," Chen Xiao's creation seems more like an affirmation of the past, particularly in those extraordinary moments. Through the use of electronic images and displays, the scenes presented may hint at the paradoxes of future existence.

It is hoped that you will be able to sense the powerful emotions and sudden moments of contemplation in Chen Xiao's artwork, where both movement and stillness may reside within your own heart.

1764822027295920128.artist_bio:
陈霄，1984年生于上海，“In Situ（在现场）”工作方式艺术家，目前生活工作于上海。先后毕业于上海大学美术学院雕塑系、法国斯特拉斯堡国立高等装饰艺术学院艺术系“Hors-Format”工作室，并获得硕士学位。作品主要以日常生活、个人经验为线索进行创作，同时对时间与物理空间的关系进行讨论。作品多以影像、装置与行为构建一个现场，显现一种游走于“边界”上的个体经验。

CHEN Xiao, (b.1984), an ‘ In Situ ’ artist, currently lives and works in Shanghai. The artist got his bachelor degree in Fine Art College of Shanghai University in Sculpture and got his master degree in Ecole supérieure des arts decoratifs de Strasbourg. The artist’s work based on daily life, personal experience and also discuss about time and physical space. The artist constructs a situation with video, installation and performance to express a personal experience of rambling by the ‘ Limit ’.

1765741388319821824.description:
司马源作品
《Symphony No.1 – PAH》
声景，18’45”，2023

团队：
司马源（概念、作曲）
王晓建（医学诊断、数据采集）
卢明（后期音效制作）

作品《Symphony No.1 – PAH》为南京大学“万籁计划”艺术与声学跨学科驻地创作。

作品《Symphony No.1 – PAH》以一位患有罕见病“肺动脉高压(Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension，PAH)”的儿童的基因突变现象和临床表征，作为主要研究对象，借助声音媒介进行创作。将患者6方面的医学诊断结果进行数据可视化，包括将DNA、mRNA、 Protein序列的编码，以“映射（mapping）”规则，严格对应至不同音高；根据心脏超声影像的脉动规律，创作打击乐节奏；以及根据肺动脉导管检测波形图的峰值与谷值，用键盘弹奏旋律等。将每种诊断数据分别设置成一个特定的声部，并将“病变前后”的特征用不同音色表现，最终成曲。

作品《Symphony No.1 – PAH》，将使更多观众通过作品直观地了解疾病的潜在机制，也使不幸罹患肺动脉高压的人群得到关注。此外，本作品颠覆性地将遗传学与声学相结合，用“实验交响”的形式消解了人们对病痛的恐惧。同时，引发观者对生命、疾病和死亡，这一内在关系的思考与探索。

（注：本项目对儿童患者数据的使用已经监管人同意和授权；聆听本作品请佩戴耳机。）

Work of SIMA Yuan
< SYMPHONY No.1 - PAH>
Soundscape, 18'45 ", 2023

Team:
SIMA Yuan (concept, composition)
WANG Xiaojian (medical diagnosis, data collection)
LU Ming (post- production)

The work Symphony No.1- PAH is powered by /0000 SOUNDERS PROJECT of Nanjing University.

The work Symphony No.1- PAH focuses on the genetic mutation phenomenon and clinical manifestations of a child with a rare disease called pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and uses sound as the material. It visualizes the medical diagnosis results of the patient in six aspects, including strictly mapping the encoding of DNA, mRNA, and Protein sequences to different notes, creating percussion rhythms based on the pulsating patterns of ultrasonic cardiogram video and creating keyboard melodies based on the peak and valley values on the pulmonary artery pressure waveform. The artist sets each type of diagnostic data as a specific voice and present the features before and after the lesion with different timbres, ultimately forming a symphony.

The work Symphony No.1- PAH will enable more audience to intuitively understand the underlying mechanisms of the disease through the work and draw attention to patients who unfortunately suffer from PAH. In addition, this work subversively combines genetics with acoustics, dispelling people's fear of illness in the form of experimental symphony. At the same time, it triggers the audience to ponder and explore the internal relationship between life, disease and death.

(Note: The use of child patient data in this work has been approved and authorized by the legal guardian. Please wear headphones to listen to this work.)

关于艺术家：

司马源，具有科学与艺术双重教育背景的艺术家。十年钢琴弹奏经验。水头电台联合创始人。生于北京，先后毕业于南京大学生命科学学院和伦敦艺术大学传媒学院。获理学学士、艺术学硕士。她的作品曾在声音艺术博物馆、TELESCOPE、南京艺术学院美术馆、意大利威尼斯策展研究学院 G21 项目、英国 FORMAT 国际摄影节、挪威卡布索美术馆、英国中央圣马丁艺术与设计学院等地展出，涉及声音、实验剧场、影像、绘画、文字、行为、虚拟设计等多种形式。曾在北京民生现代美术馆、墨方、CHAO策划声音展览。去年获北京国际设计周IDCC设计大赛“月之城”杯虚拟形象设计一等奖。

关于跨学科合作者：

王晓建，北京协和医学院遗传学教授，中国医学科学院阜外医院研究员，国家心血管病中心、心血管疾病国家重点实验室PI。专注心肺血管病遗传及精准治疗研究，在国际高影响力期刊发表学术论文70余篇，被引用超1500次，H指数22（全国前1%），拥有6项国家发明专利。在国际上率先报道多个新的心肺血管疾病重要基因，执笔编写3部临床指南/共识，首创“肺血管病遗传门诊”，为全国数百个肺动脉高压患者和家庭提供遗传咨询和生育指导。

卢明，声音实验艺术家，独立乐手、制作人。生于河北永清，本科和硕士毕业于中央美术学院实验艺术学院。实验噪音组合 M + W创建者，YCEA 青年实验艺术小组成员，小明的房间文化传媒主理人，“河北料理”项目发起人。其作品以“空间”作为创作对象，通过不同的艺术方式持续地建造自己的“空间”，从而探讨“个体与空间”在艺术与现实领域存在的可能性。代表作品包括《小明的房间》、《河北料理》等系列作品，曾多次参加国内国际重要艺术展览。作品涉及声音、行为绘画等多种媒介的运用。

About Artist：

SIMA Yuan, artist and curator with dual educational background in science and art, 10-year piano player, co-founder of Waterhead Radio. Born in Beijing, she obtained a B.S. from Nanjing University and a M.A. from London College of Communication, University of the Arts London. Her works have been known at Sound Art Museum, TELESCOPE, AMNUA, School for Curatorial Studies Venice (Italy), FORMAT15 International Photography Festival (UK), KABUSO Art Museum (Norway), Central Saint Martins College of Art and Design (UK), etc., involving various media and forms such as soundscape, experimental theater, video, painting, literature, performance art and virtual design, etc. She has curated sound exhibitions at Beijing Minsheng Art Museum, MOCUBE and CHAO. Last year, she won the first prize in “To the Moon Virtual Image Design Tourn” at BEIJING DESIGN WEEK 2023.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
司马源的作品《Symphony No.1 - PAH》，首先来自对病患和医疗系统的关注，如何将病患的信息转化为一件声音的作品。作品需要的声场还原度很高，需要一定的设备支持，才能获得最好的体验。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于司马源的创作，是对未知，但有平行于现在的其他知识。司马源真诚的将这些信息转化为可被倾听的心声，原素材也来自病患的脉搏。作品是指向对自我认知的路径，元宇宙面向的未来，不也正是同一个方向吗？

希望你能感受到司马源作品中的真诚之爱，对其他人的温情，以及技术带来跨越认知鸿沟的欣喜。也希望你能去这样发现，那些不能转化的知识，在未来能汇集成一个有趣的整体。

Sima Yuan's artwork "Symphony No.1 - PAH" originates from his concern for patients and the healthcare system. It explores how to transform the information of patients into a sonic artwork. The piece requires a high level of sound field restoration and relies on specific equipment to achieve the best experience.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," Sima Yuan's creation represents the unknown, but it also encompasses other knowledge parallel to the present. Sima Yuan sincerely transforms this information into audible heartbeats, which serve as the source material. The artwork points towards a path of self-awareness, and isn't that the same direction towards which the Metauniverse is headed?

It is hoped that you will feel the genuine love and warmth towards others in Sima Yuan's artwork, as well as the joy of bridging the cognitive gap brought about by technology. It is also hoped that you will discover that even the knowledge that cannot be transformed may converge into an interesting whole in the future.

1765677559665790976.description:
我们特地挑选了一些社交网络常见的水果表情符号，将其进行了马赛克效果处理后置入于一个立方体的六个面，随着立方体的不断旋转，水果表情符号也不断变化，从而构成了一个水果立方表情。我们将这个表情的塑造视为明天见组合一次探索二次元与三维边界的视觉造型实验，并希望透过其中一些代表深圳和南方特色的水果表情符号，向虚拟与现实边界越加模糊的今日世界传递一个明天见式的祝福。
We curated a selection of popular fruit emoticons from social media, applied a mosaic effect to them, and arranged them on the six faces of a cube. As the cube rotates, the fruit emoticons continuously change, thus constructing a fruit cubic emoticon. The emoticon-making is seeyoutomorrow’s experiment in visual plastic art, delving into the boundary between ACG and three-dimensional space. With emoticons of characteristic fruits in Shenzhen and South China, we attempt to extend a seeyoutomorrow-style greeting to today’s world, where the boundary between virtuality and reality is increasingly blurred.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
明天见的作品《水果立方表情》系列，来自于网络的表情符号，带有网络迷因文化（meme culture）基因，又类似哲学家说的“骰子一掷”。正是这两个因素构成了这系列作品的线索。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于明天见小组的创作，是游戏感的释放，轻描淡写的人生观。

希望你能感受到明天见小组的合作之轻松愉快，有时候艺术不一定有太多深意，有时候艺术也可以就是这样骰子一掷的痛快淋漓。

The artwork series "Fruit Cubic Emoticon" by the group "See You Tomorrow" draws from internet emoticons and carries the genetic code of meme culture. It also resembles what philosophers refer to as "throwing the dice." These two factors form the clues of this series.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," the creation of the "See You Tomorrow" group represents the release of a playful and lighthearted perspective on life. It exudes a sense of gamification.

It is hoped that you will feel the enjoyable and relaxed collaboration of the "See You Tomorrow" group through their artwork. Sometimes, art doesn't necessarily have profound meaning, and sometimes art can simply be the exhilarating act of throwing the dice.

1765677559665790976.artist_bio:
明天见是滕斐、黄扬、梁荣三人组成的艺术组合，他们各自从事于当代艺术、音乐策划、平面设计、摄影影像、视觉艺术等领域，以多元跨文化的视角不断观察艺术与当下社会及生活周边的相互关系和影响，再创作出对应的作品。明天见近期参与的艺术项目：“打开的窗户”，OCT-LOFT公共艺术展，华侨城创意文化园，2021年；“艺术生成艺术”，ONE ART湾汇艺术季，深圳湾一号南广场，2022年；第十届“艺术深圳”户外公共艺术项目，深圳会展中心，2023年。
seeyoutomorrow is an art group formed by Teng Fei, Huang Yang, and Liang Rong. They have individually engaged in contemporary art, music curation, graphic design, photography and videography, and visual art. From a diverse, cross-cultural perspective, the group has observed the interrelation and interaction between art and social reality and life, contributing works in response to the observations. Recently, seeyoutomorrow has participated in the following art projects: The Open Windows, OCT-LOFT Public Art Exhibition, OCT-Loft, 2021; Art Becoming Art, ONE ART, South Square, One Shenzhen Bay, 2022; Outdoor Public Art Program, The 10th Art Shenzhen, Shenzhen Convention and Exhibition Center, 2023.

1764583352708501504.description: I engaged in conversations with the homeless on the streets of Germany and conducted 3D scans of them. Using digital information technology, I replicated their physical appearances. By examining their clothing, skin condition, and the items they carried, one can glean insights into their life experiences. Each person is born with a physical form, and as life circumstances and experiences change, so does the external manifestation of that form.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
张翀的《From East Hellweg street to West Hellweg street》系列，是技术和人的讨论，艺术家置自己于：社会内在运作，人的阶层现实，和人的物理形态之讨论中。最终作品如同巨大的偶戏中，可被穿戴的外壳。更进一步讨论，外在的差异，及其内在人性的冲突。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于张翀存在着双重悖论，张翀设问的和社会实践的，恰是人类未来的困境。可被数据化的，可被拟态的，可被入侵的。艺术家形成这一过程的镜像关系，或隐于技术之后，却也在共享这一困境。

希望张翀的作品，能让你对人类有同情心，对自己的未来有希望，相信技术带来的，并非只有绝望，还有人类天性的游戏感，还有彼此映照的瞬间，拥抱科技，不放弃对人性的追问。

Zhang Chong's series "From East Hellweg Street to West Hellweg Street" is a discussion on technology and humanity. The artist places himself in the discourse of societal inner workings, the social hierarchy, and the physical forms of people. The final artwork is like a large puppet show, a wearable shell. It further explores the external differences and the internal conflicts of human nature.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," there exists a dual paradox for Zhang Chong. The questions he raises and the societal practices he interrogates precisely reflect the dilemmas of humanity's future. The ability to be data-driven, to be simulated, and to be invaded. The artist forms a mirrored relationship within this process, sometimes hidden behind technology, yet still sharing in this predicament.

It is hoped that Zhang Chong's work will evoke sympathy for humanity and instill hope for one's own future. It encourages belief that technology brings not only despair but also a sense of playfulness inherent in human nature and moments of reflection upon each other. Embracing technology, don't give up on questioning human nature.

1764583352708501504.artist_bio: ZHANG Chong, born in Zhejiang in 1988. Graduated with a master’s degree and the title of Professor Jochen Breme’s Meisterschüler from the Alanus University of Arts and Social Sciences, Germany, in 2018. Now works and lives in Shanghai. His works have been exhibited in the Museum Kunstpalast in Dusseldorf, in the art fair contemporary art ruhr (C.A.R.), and other art spaces in Shanghai, Shenzhen, Germany, the Netherlands and etc. His works involve the combination of various materials, often characterized by a literary and narrative quality in the creative process.

1764579476303384576.description: I engaged in conversations with the homeless on the streets of Germany and conducted 3D scans of them. Using digital information technology, I replicated their physical appearances. By examining their clothing, skin condition, and the items they carried, one can glean insights into their life experiences. Each person is born with a physical form, and as life circumstances and experiences change, so does the external manifestation of that form.

comments.name: 李振华 - Li Zhenhua
comments.comment:
张翀的《From East Hellweg street to West Hellweg street》系列，是技术和人的讨论，艺术家置自己于：社会内在运作，人的阶层现实，和人的物理形态之讨论中。最终作品如同巨大的偶戏中，可被穿戴的外壳。更进一步讨论，外在的差异，及其内在人性的冲突。

《元宇宙的领航员们》的命题，之于张翀存在着双重悖论，张翀设问的和社会实践的，恰是人类未来的困境。可被数据化的，可被拟态的，可被入侵的。艺术家形成这一过程的镜像关系，或隐于技术之后，却也在共享这一困境。

希望张翀的作品，能让你对人类有同情心，对自己的未来有希望，相信技术带来的，并非只有绝望，还有人类天性的游戏感，还有彼此映照的瞬间，拥抱科技，不放弃对人性的追问。

Zhang Chong's series "From East Hellweg Street to West Hellweg Street" is a discussion on technology and humanity. The artist places himself in the discourse of societal inner workings, the social hierarchy, and the physical forms of people. The final artwork is like a large puppet show, a wearable shell. It further explores the external differences and the internal conflicts of human nature.

In the context of "Navigators of the Metaverse," there exists a dual paradox for Zhang Chong. The questions he raises and the societal practices he interrogates precisely reflect the dilemmas of humanity's future. The ability to be data-driven, to be simulated, and to be invaded. The artist forms a mirrored relationship within this process, sometimes hidden behind technology, yet still sharing in this predicament.

It is hoped that Zhang Chong's work will evoke sympathy for humanity and instill hope for one's own future. It encourages belief that technology brings not only despair but also a sense of playfulness inherent in human nature and moments of reflection upon each other. Embracing technology, don't give up on questioning human nature.
